meta.edition: Thucydides. Historiae, Vol 1-2. Jones, Henry Stuart, editor. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1910. (1942 printing).

variants_available.name: xyn
variants_available.evidence: A 12.790/1k -> B 12.851/1k (A/B 1.00): PARITY, the clearest systemic imitation in the set and invisible to a rarity filter
variants_available.caveat: ξυνός is excluded: it stands to κοινός, not to συν-.

variants_available.name: gign
variants_available.summary: Attic reduplicated γιγν- for Koine γιν-
variants_available.caveat: Exact: no other Greek word contains γιγν (γίγας has γιγα). The reverse direction is NOT applied — Αἴγινα, Ῥήγιον, Οὐιττιγίς would all become forms of γίγνομαι.

variants_available.name: tt
variants_available.evidence: A 0.068/1k -> B 0.485/1k (A/B 0.14): EXCESS, B is 7.1x A — this rule runs opposite to the others
variants_available.caveat: Marked side is the LATER Atticist restoration, not Thucydides' usage. 64% of B's raw ττ tokens are proper nouns (Οὐιττιγίς 116 = the Gothic king Witigis, Ῥήγιον, Σίττας), and POOLING them is merge-harmless but visible: Οὐιττιγίς pools to Οὐισσιγίς, which is no word. The proper-noun filter is load-bearing for this rule, not a nicety.

variants_available.name: rr
variants_available.caveat: Polluted on all sides: Thucydides' ρρ is Ἀρράβαιον (proper) and ἐπερρώσθησαν (prefix assimilation), his ρσ is χερσίν (< χείρ, inflection) and Περσῶν. Pooling only.
